parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a detailed follow-up within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a potential safety risk for their model; when there is an immediate danger, they must issue an urgent customer warning without delay.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a detailed follow-up within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a potential safety risk for their model; when there is an immediate danger, they must issue an urgent customer warning without delay.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a detailed follow-up within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a potential safety risk for their model; when there is an immediate danger, they must issue an urgent customer warning without delay. Reports must include the model, incident date and location, known consequences, and steps taken. Manufacturers must maintain records and promptly correct incomplete reports.

parameters.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a corrective-action plan and undergo retesting; the regulator may impose proportionate restrictions or additional safeguards based on the results and other safety evidence. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit continued or new sales while the manufacturer implements an approved plan, unless the regulator determines that restriction is necessary to address an unreasonable safety risk.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a corrective-action plan and undergo retesting; the regulator may impose proportionate restrictions or additional safeguards based on the results and other safety evidence. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit continued or new sales while the manufacturer implements an approved plan, unless the regulator determines that restriction is necessary to address an unreasonable safety risk.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55°C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, including sample size and failure rate, to the regulator and make those results available to current and prospective customers of that model. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a corrective-action plan and undergo retesting; the regulator may impose proportionate restrictions or additional safeguards based on the results and other safety evidence. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit continued or new sales while the manufacturer implements an approved plan, unless the regulator determines that restriction is necessary to address an unreasonable safety risk.

parameters.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support it, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency isolation measure, within six years after adoption. The regulator may approve a documented, technically justified alternative where retrofit is infeasible, provided equivalent protection is maintained and affected customers are informed.

parameters.quote: All new units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The regulator may approve an alternative design that provides equivalent or greater fire protection, based on documented testing.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The regulator may approve an alternative design that provides equivalent or greater fire protection, based on documented testing.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The regulator may approve an alternative design that provides equivalent or greater fire protection, based on documented testing. Manufacturers must inform customers of the protection provided and any relevant limitations.

parameters.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model's verified annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units. Manufacturers must notify the regulator and affected customers without delay, stop sales and deployment of the affected model, and implement the regulator-approved recall and remedy.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A recall is mandatory when a model's verified annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units. Manufacturers must notify the regulator and affected customers without delay, stop sales and deployment of the affected model, and implement the regulator-approved recall and remedy.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices describing relevant hazards, precautions, and reporting channels, and must promptly notify affected customers of material new safety information. A recall is mandatory when a model’s verified annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units. Calculate the rate from distinct thermal incidents attributable to that model during a consistent annual reporting period, divided by that model’s installed units during the same period and expressed per 100,000 units. Include incidents whether or not they were initially reported to a regulator; maintain auditable incident and unit records, explain the calculation, and make supporting records available to the regulator for verification. Manufacturers must notify the regulator and affected customers without delay, stop sales and deployment of the affected model, and implement the regulator-approved recall and remedy. The regulator may require a recall or other protective action below this threshold when the evidence indicates an unreasonable safety risk.

judge_section_notes: The final S2 removes any automatic sales stop above 5%, leaves per-model rates open to customers on request without public publication, and has no sunset on the over-limit allowance, which favours Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition or interim trigger, which bites on Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), and S3's six-year retrofit window matches Northwind's red line and suits its 38% shut-off coverage. S1 is strong (24-hour reporting covering all thermal incidents, which closes the unreported-incident gap for both companies), and S4 sets built-in suppression at 36 months, which suits Halcyon's cost position.
